title: Sound & Volume
source: Science G3 B2 Study sheet pp.12-16; Worksheet Q10

scenes.t: Sound is made of vibrations. Vibration means moving back and forth very fast.
When an object vibrates, it makes sound waves. The waves travel through the air to reach our ears.
Violin strings vibrate when you pluck them. A drum skin vibrates when you hit it.
Xylophone bars vibrate when you hit them. The air inside a trumpet vibrates when you blow into it.
Volume is how loud or quiet a sound is. Bigger vibrations make louder sounds. Smaller vibrations make quieter sounds.
We can change the volume by changing the force. Hit a drum strongly for a loud sound, and gently for a quiet sound.
We can also change the distance. The closer you are to the sound source, the louder it is. The further away, the quieter it is.

activities.title: Loud or Quiet?
activities.prompt: Will the sound be LOUD or QUIET?

why.l: More force or closer distance makes bigger vibrations.
why.q: Less force or further distance makes it quieter.

activities.title: Dancing Rice Drum
activities.goal: See sound vibrations and test loud vs quiet.

predict.q: When you bang the pot harder, the rice will jump…

steps.t: Stretch the cling film tightly over the bowl and hold it with the rubber band. This is your drum.
Put a few grains of rice on top of the cling film.
Hold the pot close to the bowl and tap it gently with the spoon. Watch the rice.
Now bang the pot harder. Then try again standing further away.

activities.result: The rice jumps when you make a sound. A louder bang makes it jump higher, and from further away it jumps less.
activities.why: Sound waves make the cling film vibrate. Bigger vibrations mean a louder sound, and sound gets quieter with distance.
